The sun hung low over the horizon, painting the sky in stripes of gold and pink. Birds chirped lazily as they flitted between branches, their wings casting tiny shadows on the grass below. A gentle breeze rustled the leaves, carrying with it the scent of damp earth and wildflowers.

I sat on a weathered wooden bench, my feet dangling over the edge, watching the world go by. The street was quiet, just a few cars passing in the distance, their headlights flickering like distant stars. A cat with a mottled coat lounged nearby, its eyes half-closed, as if it had seen enough of the day already.

I thought about the things I’d done today—coffee with a friend, a walk in the park, a book I’d started but not finished. Life was simple, really. The kind of simple that felt heavy with possibility, like the air before a storm. But storms didn’t always bring rain; sometimes they just brought a clearer sky.

I closed my eyes for a moment, letting the warmth of the sun and the coolness of the breeze wrap around me. It was enough. Just enough.
